h1:
7 Hostel-Style Stays
in Pattaya, Chonburi
That We've Reviewed
heroSub: 7 hand-picked hostel- and poshtel-style stays in Pattaya (plus one beachfront resort on the eastern coast) that we've reviewed in depth — central and walk to the beach, or quiet over on the Jomtien side, with everything from a few-hundred-baht dorm bed to a private room with its own bathroom. Prices from around ฿280–2,300/night.
introH2: 🎒 How many kinds of hostel-style stays does Pattaya have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: These days, "hostel" in Pattaya no longer means bunk beds packed together and a long row of shared bathrooms, and that's what makes choosing a budget stay here more fun than you'd expect — some are central hostels a few minutes' walk from Pattaya Beach for a few hundred baht; some are poshtels over on the Jomtien side, set back a little so it's quieter and you sleep better; and some give you a private room with its own bathroom and hot water at dorm prices. A lot of people book a budget stay and end up with a location or vibe that doesn't match their trip, and feel it wasn't worth it. This article rounds up 7 hostel-style stays in Pattaya (plus one beachfront resort on the eastern coast) that we've reviewed in depth, across Central Pattaya, Jomtien, Pratamnak and Chao Lao Beach — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you the upsides and the honest caveats alike, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links for all of them.
mrtHtml: Pattaya has no metro, but getting around town is easy with the songthaew (red baht bus) that loops the main roads for a few baht, or you can hail a Grab or a motorbike taxi. From U-Tapao Airport (UTP) it's about 40–45 min into town; from Suvarnabhumi it's around 1.5–2 hours depending on traffic. The areas in this article: Central Pattaya — the city centre, walk to the beach and CentralFestival, busy day and night · Jomtien — the quieter southern side, with a night market and a long beach, good if you want to relax · Pratamnak / Nong Taphao, Thappraya Road — near the viewpoints and the pier to Koh Larn, you'll need a car · Chao Lao Beach, Tha Mai, Chanthaburi — on the eastern coast outside Pattaya, quiet and you'll need your own car.

entries.name: The Bedrooms Hostel Pattaya
entries.badge: 🏖️ 3-min walk to the beach · highest score
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Beach Road Soi 1 · 220 m from Pattaya Beach
entries.addr: 436/60 Moo 9, Pattaya Beach Soi 1, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If you had to pick the budget stay with the best-value location of these 7, plenty of reviews would name The Bedrooms Hostel Pattaya first — a 2-star hostel on Beach Road Soi 1 in Central Pattaya, just about 220 metres from Pattaya Beach, roughly a 3-min walk, and the highest score in this article at 9.1 from 249 reviews on Trip.com · The thing guests agree on is the location: if you wake up wanting a stroll by the sea you can do it right away without calling a ride, and within walking distance there are restaurants, convenience stores and songthaew stops everywhere · It has a 10-bed female dorm, a 12-bed male dorm and private rooms, with air-con in every room that guests call nicely cool, comfortable beds, and many reviews saying the rooms are cleaner than the price suggests · A rare extra is free private parking in central Pattaya, plus a shared kitchen, a bar, a massage room, luggage storage and a 24-hour reception · The honest caveats from the reviews: it's a hostel on the lively beach road, busy all night, and rooms facing the street pick up some noise from people coming back late and the road itself, especially Friday–Saturday nights; rooms are fairly small as hostels go, there's no pool, and you should know that even the private rooms still share a bathroom with others · Best for solo travellers, pairs and groups of friends on a budget who want a central location for a few hundred baht and plan to use the stay mainly as a place to sleep and shower.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room away from the street or on a quieter floor when you book, and pack earplugs for the night · If you're driving, mention the free parking ahead of time, as spaces are limited when it's full.
pros: Central Pattaya location, 3-min walk to the beach, highest score in the article at 9.1
Beds and rooms cleaner than the price suggests, comfortable beds, air-con in every room
Free private parking, rare for a central hostel
Shared kitchen, massage room, luggage storage, 24-hour reception
cons: On the beach road, you hear next-door rooms and the street at night
Small rooms, as hostels go · no pool
Even private rooms still share a bathroom with others (from reviews)

entries.name: Sindy's Hostel Pattaya
entries.addr: 78/101 Pattaya Soi 2, Pattaya 2nd Road, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: Among Pattaya's budget stays, if you go by sheer number of reviews, Sindy's Hostel Pattaya is the most reviewed in this article — Agoda has it at 9.1 overall from over 611 reviews, and Trip.com sits around 8.7, with location its highest-scoring category · It's a roughly 18-room 2-star hostel on Pattaya Soi 2 (Pattaya Second Road), sitting right in the city centre — about a 5-min walk to Central Marina, 8 min to Terminal 21 and 15 min to Pattaya Beach, with hundreds of restaurants all around · What sets Sindy's apart from similarly priced hostels is the American-style breakfast, which many call tastier and more varied than expected (but check whether your rate includes it or you pay around ฿200 per person extra, as it differs by platform) · There's everything from a 10-bed shared dorm with curtains and personal sockets to Single, Twin and family rooms, all air-conditioned — a big deal in Pattaya, where it's hot most of the year · The most repeated strength is the staff, who guests describe as friendly and proactive, recommending restaurants, arranging transfers and setting up Koh Larn tours · The honest caveats: it's a fairly old building, rooms are small and some are very minimal, there's no lift, no pool or on-site parking, and Pattaya Soi 2 has a nightlife scene, so some nights you'll hear noise in rooms facing the street · Best for solo travellers, backpackers and couples on a budget who want staff that go out of their way to help.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check the breakfast terms clearly — whether it's in the rate or costs extra · If you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room not facing the street or on the innermost floor, and make use of the reception for Koh Larn tours and transfers.
pros: Most reviewed in the article, Agoda 9.1 from 611 reviews
Free breakfast that's tastier than expected · shared kitchen to cook your own
Central location, walk to Central Marina and Terminal 21
Friendly staff who help book tours and transfers (from reviews)
cons: Old building, small rooms, no lift
No pool or on-site parking
Pattaya Soi 2 has a nightlife scene, some nights you hear noise in street-facing rooms

entries.name: Happy Hostel Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Soi Chaloem Phrakiat 21/1 · 10-min walk to CentralFestival
entries.addr: 332/9 Moo 9, Soi Chaloem Phrakiat 21/1, Pattaya Sai 3 Road, Nongprue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: Where the two central hostels above sell their beachfront location, Happy Hostel Pattaya sells what budget travellers look for but rarely find — quiet, and a good night's sleep · It's a 2-star hostel on Soi Chaloem Phrakiat 21/1 in Central Pattaya, set back from the beach road far enough to feel like a residential soi rather than the nightlife zone, so you don't sleep to the sound of bars and motorbikes all night, yet you can still walk to CentralFestival in about 10 min and Pattaya Beach in about 15 min · What sets it apart from similarly priced hostels is the set of facilities you get at dorm prices — an indoor pool, a shared kitchen and self-service washing machines all in one place, where many at the same price have no pool · There's a 6-bed shared dorm from around ฿300/night, plus private air-con Single, Twin and Double rooms with their own bathroom, a TV and a fridge · Top of the reviews is cleanliness — many say everything looks new and well kept — plus friendly staff and a high service score of around 8.9 · The honest caveats from the reviews: there's no breakfast, so you plan your own or use the shared kitchen; pool upkeep is inconsistent at times according to some reviews; the safety category on some platforms isn't as high as the others; and being deep in the soi means you'll call a ride back late from the beach zone · Best for solo travellers on a budget, long-stayers and remote workers who want cleanliness, quiet and a pool to cool off in.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Save the pin for Soi Chaloem Phrakiat 21/1 ahead of time, as it's a side soi and easier to find than walking around looking · There's no breakfast — use the shared kitchen and buy ingredients to cook, which saves money, especially on a long stay.
pros: Quiet, easier to sleep than the beach zone, but a 10-min walk to CentralFestival
Indoor pool, shared kitchen and washing machine, all at dorm prices
Cleanliness near the top of the praise, many say everything looks new
Friendly staff, high service score around 8.9
cons: No breakfast, you plan your own
Deep in the soi, you call a ride back late from the beach zone
Pool upkeep inconsistent at times according to some reviews

entries.name: Jellyfish Hostel Pattaya
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.7 · up to 9.6 on some platforms
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Jomtien Soi 2 · a few minutes' walk to the beach

rooms.type: Double Room with Balcony (~30 sq m)

entries.addr: 144/138 Moo 12, Jomtien Beach Soi 2, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If the word "hostel" makes you picture bunk beds packed together and a long row of shared bathrooms, Jellyfish Hostel Pattaya is a different thing — it's a small roughly 8-room guesthouse on Jomtien Soi 2 where most rooms are private with their own bathroom and hot water at hostel prices · That's why many pick it over a central dorm, getting privacy and a private bathroom on a budget that's still light · It's on Jomtien Soi 2, on the southern side of Pattaya that's quieter than the centre, a few minutes' walk to Jomtien Beach, with Jomtien's restaurants and street food all around · Rooms range from the Cozy Double, a compact twin-bed room of about 10 sq m, up to the Double Room with Balcony at about 30 sq m with a private balcony, and a Family Room for families or small groups of friends · Real reviews agree on the cleanliness, the strong hot water, the cool air-con and the friendly staff, plus extras like a shared kitchen, a lounge, bikes to borrow and free coffee and tea · The score is around 8.7 on Trip.com and as high as 9.6 on some platforms · The honest caveats: it's a small place with few rooms, the entry-level rooms are fairly compact and better for sleeping than spending the whole day in, there's no pool, and the review count on some platforms is still modest · Best for couples or solo travellers who want a quiet private room with its own bathroom on the Jomtien side at a price you can still reach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For more space and a balcony, pick the Double Room with Balcony over the compact entry-level room · It has few rooms here, so it fills up fast in high season and on long weekends — book ahead.
pros: Private rooms with their own bathroom and hot water at hostel prices
Jomtien side is quieter than central Pattaya, a few minutes' walk to the beach
Clean, cool air-con, strong hot water, friendly staff (from reviews)
Shared kitchen, lounge, bikes to borrow and free coffee and tea
cons: Few rooms, fills up fast in high season
Entry-level rooms are compact · no pool
Review count on some platforms is still modest

entries.name: Travel Light Hostel Pattaya
entries.badge: 🌇 Rooftop with a kitchen + distant sea view
tags: 🚗 Near the pier to Koh Larn
entries.addr: 855 Thappraya Road, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: To be straight with you, Travel Light Hostel Pattaya is a stay we've included with an honest warning label — a small 2-star hostel on Thappraya Road in the Pratamnak / Nong Taphao area on the southern side of Pattaya, with just a few rooms, both mixed dorm beds and air-con family rooms with a flat-screen TV · What many like, and what's genuinely its charm, is the rooftop with a shared kitchen and a distant sea view — a quiet, easy-going spot, good for hanging out and cooking in the evening, and a corner many guests photograph and bring back · It's near several southern attractions — the Pratamnak Hill viewpoint about a 5–7 min drive, Jomtien Beach about a 5 min drive, Bali Hai Pier (the pier to Koh Larn) about a 5–8 min drive, and Walking Street about a 7–10 min drive · But to be honest, the real review scores are still mixed — 6.0/10 on Trip.com and 3.0/5 on Tripadvisor from not many reviews, with complaints about inconsistent service, cleanliness in some spots, and a location off the beach that means a car every time you head out · Prices start at around ฿500/night for a dorm bed and around ฿900 for a family room, which is light for a private air-con room · So we don't rate it as a sure-thing like the top three, but it keeps a spot on the list for people who have a car, set their expectations to the price, and value the rooftop and the quiet of South Pattaya over a beachfront location · Before you book, read the latest guest reviews and pick a free-cancellation rate in case plans change.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's off the beach here and the score is still mixed, so it suits people with their own car · Read the latest reviews before booking and pick a free-cancellation rate in case plans change.
pros: Rooftop with a shared kitchen and a distant sea view, quiet atmosphere
Cheap air-con rooms, both dorm and family rooms
Near the Pratamnak Hill viewpoint and the pier to Koh Larn
Suits budget travellers with their own car
cons: Real review scores still mixed, Trip.com 6.0 · Tripadvisor 3.0/5
Complaints about service and cleanliness in some spots (from reviews)
Location off the beach, you need a car · few reviews

entries.type: Beach Resort 3★ · Chao Lao Beach, Chanthaburi
entries.name: Villa Cha Cha Chaolao Beach Resort
entries.badge: 🌊 On Chao Lao Beach · highest score
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · Tha Mai, Chanthaburi (car needed)
entries.addr: 3/10 Moo 6, Chao Lao Beach Road, Khlong Khut, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: On a list of budget hostel-style stays, Villa Cha Cha Chaolao Beach Resort is the option that steps up into a different lane — it's not a hostel but a 3-star beach resort right on Chao Lao Beach, in Khlong Khut, Tha Mai District, Chanthaburi, on an eastern coast many people overlook · We've included it for those who want to upgrade from a city dorm to a private seaside room on a budget that isn't too steep · What makes it interesting is that it's a resort that opened in 2023 and was renovated in 2024, so the rooms are still new and clean, with both bungalows and suite cabanas, and some, like the Beach Front Family, look out over the sea from the balcony · There's an outdoor beachfront pool, a sauna, a seafood restaurant and a barbecue area, with the quiet feel of a beach that isn't crowded yet · Real reviews give it a high 9.7 from 11 reviews on Trip.com, praising the new rooms, the cleanliness and the privacy by the beach · Opening your door in the morning to a sea breeze and the soft sound of waves is something a central Pattaya dorm can't give you · The honest caveats: the location is fairly far outside Pattaya, a few hours' drive from Bangkok but you need your own car, as getting around the resort on foot isn't convenient; the facilities aren't extensive like a big resort; and there aren't many reviews yet since it just opened · Best for couples or families with a car who want a quiet seaside stay on the eastern coast, in a new room at an accessible price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: You need your own car here, as it's outside Pattaya on Chao Lao Beach in Chanthaburi · For a sea view from the balcony, pick a Beach Front room, and book ahead on long weekends.
pros: On Chao Lao Beach with a beachfront pool, quiet atmosphere
Opened 2023, renovated 2024, rooms still new and clean, scoring 9.7
Private seaside rooms at an accessible price, some with a sea view
Seafood restaurant, sauna and a barbecue area
cons: Outside Pattaya, on the Chanthaburi side, you need your own car
Facilities not extensive like a big resort
Just opened, not many reviews yet

entries.name: JN9 Poshtel Pattaya
entries.badge: 🌙 Quiet · near the beach and night market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Soi Jomtien 9 · near the beach and night market
tags: 🏖️ Walk to the beach + night market
entries.addr: 344/169 Moo 12, Soi Jomtien 9, Nongprue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: We close the list with another Jomtien-side option focused on comfort on a budget — JN9 Poshtel Pattaya is a small poshtel-style stay on Soi Jomtien 9, for people who want to escape the bustle of central Pattaya for a quieter side while still being able to walk to the beach and the night market · It's a small place of around 9–10 rooms, with both private rooms with a balcony and shared dorm beds, all with cool air-con, a TV and free Wi-Fi · "Poshtel" means a hostel polished to look and feel a step nicer than the average dorm, and that's how this one positions itself — with an in-house café and restaurant, plus free parking, which helps a lot if you're driving · From Soi Jomtien 9 it's a few minutes' walk to Jomtien Beach, Dongtan Beach and the Jomtien night market, while Bali Hai Pier (the pier to Koh Larn) is about a 10 min drive · Real reviews praise the quiet, the cleanliness and the friendly staff, with a score of 8.4 from 142 reviews on Trip.com, a good review count for a small stay · Prices start at around ฿450/night for a dorm bed, with a Deluxe room with a balcony and its own bathroom around ฿850 · The honest caveats: it's a small place with limited facilities, no pool, some Standard Double rooms still use a shared bathroom, and on the Jomtien side you need a car to get into central Pattaya or Walking Street · Best for those who want a quiet, budget stay on the Jomtien side and can live with limited facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For an own bathroom and a balcony, pick the Deluxe Room, as some Standard Double rooms still use a shared bathroom · It has free parking, good for those driving to the Jomtien side.
pros: Quiet Jomtien side, walk to the beach and night market
Free parking and an in-house café · every room with air-con and free Wi-Fi
Clean, friendly staff, scoring 8.4 from 142 reviews
Deluxe rooms have a balcony and their own bathroom at a light price
cons: Small stay, limited facilities, no pool
Some Standard Double rooms still use a shared bathroom
Jomtien side, you need a car for central Pattaya or Walking Street

advice.head: Want a private room with its own bathroom, on a budget

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are starting estimates from the standard room range and may change by date and season — always check the real price and compare 3 sites before booking · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms, not from staying ourselves · Travel Light Hostel's review scores are still mixed (Trip.com 6.0 · Tripadvisor 3.0/5), so read the latest reviews and pick a free-cancellation rate before booking · Villa Cha Cha Chaolao Beach Resort is on Chao Lao Beach in Tha Mai, Chanthaburi (outside Pattaya), and you need your own car · Most budget stays are small places, and in high season (November–February), on long weekends, at Songkran and New Year, prices rise and rooms sell out fast, so book ahead · Pattaya has no metro — the songthaew or Grab is easy; from U-Tapao Airport it's about 40–45 min into town · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — common questions travellers ask about hostel-style stays in Pattaya

faq.q: ❓ What's the best hostel-style stay in Pattaya?
faq.a: It depends on your trip · For location and value, The Bedrooms Hostel Pattaya ฿280 is a 3-min walk to the beach with a 9.1, the highest score in the hostel group · For review count and breakfast, Sindy's Hostel has the most reviews, Agoda 9.1 from 611 reviews · For quiet and a pool, Happy Hostel · For a private room with its own bathroom, Jellyfish Hostel · And for a quiet stay on the Jomtien side with parking, JN9 Poshtel

faq.q: ❓ How much does a hostel in Pattaya cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at around ฿280–2,300 per night · The cheapest are dorm beds — The Bedrooms from ฿280, Happy Hostel ฿300 and Sindy's ฿390 · For a private room with its own bathroom, Jellyfish starts at ฿750 and JN9 Deluxe around ฿850 · Villa Cha Cha is a beachfront resort from ฿2,300 · All prices are starting estimates from standard rooms, and during festivals prices can run higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in for a hostel in Pattaya?
faq.a: Central Pattaya suits people who want to walk to the beach and the malls, busy day and night (The Bedrooms, Sindy's, Happy Hostel) · Jomtien suits people who want it quieter, with a night market and a long beach (Jellyfish, JN9 Poshtel) · Pratamnak / Nong Taphao is near the pier to Koh Larn but you need a car (Travel Light) · And Chao Lao Beach, Chanthaburi suits people with a car who want a stay by the eastern coast (Villa Cha Cha)

faq.q: ❓ Which hostel in Pattaya has private rooms with their own bathroom?
faq.a: The clearest option is Jellyfish Hostel Pattaya ฿750, where most private rooms have their own bathroom and hot water · Next is Happy Hostel, with private air-con rooms with their own bathroom from around ฿600, and JN9 Poshtel, whose Deluxe rooms have a balcony and their own bathroom around ฿850 · The Bedrooms and Sindy's focus on dorm beds and private rooms that mostly still use a shared bathroom

faq.q: ❓ Which hostel in Pattaya is quiet and good for sleeping?
faq.a: To avoid the bar noise at night, Happy Hostel Pattaya on Soi Chaloem Phrakiat is set back from the beach road, quiet and with an indoor pool · On the Jomtien side, JN9 Poshtel and Jellyfish Hostel are also quieter than central Pattaya · The central hostels on the beach road, like The Bedrooms and Sindy's, are livelier, so ask for a room not facing the street and pack earplugs

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Pattaya hostel?
faq.a: Most budget stays in this article are small places (around 8–18 rooms), so they fill up fast · In high season (November–February), on long weekends, at Songkran and New Year, book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, especially Jellyfish and JN9, which have few rooms · Other times 1–2 weeks is enough · Most platforms usually offer Free Cancellation, so it's worth locking in that kind of rate first if your plans aren't firm, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
